market_pulse.note: About $64,918 at 4 p.m. ET Monday, down about 0.3% over 24 hours (Market Alleys); it fell to about $62,000 on Sunday, its lowest since July 14 (CoinDesk; Zerocap).
About $1,817 at 4 p.m. ET Monday, down about 0.5% over 24 hours (Market Alleys), and down about 15% over the past week (Zerocap).
About $2.18 trillion per CoinGecko (via Cryptonomist); The Daily Coins showed about $2.20 trillion, down 0.11% over 24 hours, late Monday morning.

themes.title: Six straight weekly losses
themes.summary: Bitcoin has fallen for six consecutive weeks, its longest losing run since late February, and dropped about 14% last week (CoinDesk; Zerocap).

themes.title: Sentiment at extreme fear
themes.summary: CoinMarketCap's Fear and Greed Index fell to 12 from 19 on Friday, and the alternative.me index read 10 (CoinDesk; The Daily Coins).

themes.title: ETF outflows continue
themes.summary: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs lost about $1.91 billion over seven straight sessions, and Ether ETFs extended their outflow streak to seven weeks (CoinDesk; Zerocap).

themes.title: Leverage flushed out
themes.summary: About $2 billion of mostly long positions were liquidated over the weekend, and funding rates were negative for most coins on Monday (CoinDesk).

themes.title: Corporate holders under pressure
themes.summary: MARA sold 13,597 BTC for about $1.1 billion, and MSCI plans to remove Strategy and Metaplanet from its indexes after the Nov. 30 close (Zerocap).

categories.name: Majors (BTC/ETH)
categories.note: Both slightly lower over 24 hours by Monday's U.S. close, with Bitcoin down about 0.3% and Ether about 0.5% (Market Alleys).

categories.name: Altcoins
categories.note: Breadth was weak, with 76 of the top 100 coins lower at midday UTC; Kite, Sky and Jupiter each fell more than 5.5% in the CoinDesk 100 (The Daily Coins; CoinDesk).

categories.name: Derivatives
categories.note: Futures volume fell 47% to $139 billion and open interest was about $108 billion; the most-traded BTC options expire Nov. 27, with heavy activity at the $50,000 put strike (CoinDesk).

categories.name: Stablecoins and ETFs
categories.note: USDT and USDC saw net off-ramping last week, stablecoin supply was about $287.8 billion, and November spot BTC ETF outflows topped $2 billion (Zerocap; The Daily Coins; Cryptonomist).

watch_list.why: Zerocap cites $60,000 as support, with the July low at $58,570 below it, and the 200-week average near $67,800 as resistance; Sunday's low was about $62,000 (Zerocap; CoinDesk).
Traders are watching tech stocks closely, and Nvidia reports after the close on Nov. 17, its first results since Jensen Huang resigned (CoinDesk; Yahoo Finance).
Fed minutes are due this week with a December hike fully priced, and analysts are watching whether spot ETF outflows continue (Zerocap; Cryptonomist).
